---
title: "4. Understanding and Navigating the Data Dictionary"
---


## What you will learn

Find a field for a clinical concept, check its scope and coding over time, and build a versioned variable map that another researcher can audit.

::: {.callout-note title="Official source — verify each field"}
Start with the [release-specific PUF dictionary and legacy documents](https://www.facs.org/quality-programs/cancer-programs/national-cancer-database/puf/). The [2024 dictionary](https://www.facs.org/media/ilqb5snq/2024-data-dictionary.pdf) is revised March 2026. Match your release rather than automatically choosing the newest manual. Registry manuals contain fields that are not necessarily present in a PUF.
:::

## Search by concept, then by exact variable

**Educational explanation.** Suppose your question includes “stage.” That word alone is insufficient: you may need clinical stage before treatment, pathologic stage after surgery, or another defined staging construct. A convenient column name does not settle the scientific question.

1. Write the concept and when it should be measured relative to the exposure.
2. Search the dictionary using the concept and likely synonyms. Read the whole item entry, including notes and related fields.
3. Record the exact raw name and item identifier, where available. Do not rename raw columns in place.
4. Check which cases and diagnosis years the item applies to. Look for changes in definition, coding system, collection requirements, and missing-value conventions.
5. Identify each possible raw value's meaning using your local documentation. Keep code-like fields as strings during import.
6. Read the matching release changes and linked coding resources. A different manual's similarly named item may have a different purpose.
7. Write your proposed analytic transformation separately; request mentor or registrar review where the meaning is unresolved.
8. After authorized import, compare actual codes and year-specific frequencies with expectations. Unexpected values should trigger investigation, not automatic coercion.

## A variable map is an analysis contract

The template `variable_map.csv` is a blank metadata table, not patient data. Use one row per source field and coding era when necessary.

| Field group | What to record |
|---|---|
| Concept and raw identity | Concept, exact variable name, item ID, release |
| Source evidence | Source URL/title, revision, page/section, date checked; summarize in your own words |
| Scope | Applicable sites, diagnosis years, definition/coding changes |
| Raw representation | Data type, valid values, distinct unknown/not-applicable codes |
| Analytic decision | New name, transformation, missingness rule, model reference category |
| Review and validation | Decision rationale, reviewer, date, checks and unresolved issues |

Do not paste entire proprietary code tables into this public guide. Record pointers and the minimal original notes needed to audit your work within permitted use.

## Worked example: fictional codes

Assume an invented field `DEMO_MARKER` uses `P` for present, `A` for absent, `U` for unknown, and `N` for not applicable. These are **not NCDB codes**.

Your source notes preserve all four meanings. A project decision might produce `marker_present` with 1 for `P`, 0 for `A`, and missing for the other two. Keep a companion reason field so `U` and `N` remain distinguishable. Mapping both to numeric missing is not permission to forget their different denominators.

```python
import pandas as pd
raw = pd.Series(["P", "A", "U", "N"], dtype="string")
assert raw.isin(["P", "A", "U", "N"]).all()
analytic = raw.map({"P": 1, "A": 0}).astype("Int64")
reason = raw.map({"U": "unknown", "N": "not applicable"})
```

If a new value `X` appears, stop and establish its meaning. Do not convert every unrecognized code to missing silently.

## Build an availability matrix

For each required field, make a row for each diagnosis year or documented era. Distinguish **collected and applicable**, **not collected**, **not applicable**, and **uncertain**. Then inspect observed missingness within the applicable cases. An empty column before collection began is structural unavailability; it is not ordinary sporadic missingness.

**Project decision.** If the exposure is unavailable for part of the proposed period, choose a justified restriction, a documented harmonization, or a revised question. Do not invent an equivalent field or impute an unmeasured historical construct without methodological review.

## Practice and readiness

Complete a map entry for one required concept, including source revision, years, missing codes, a proposed transformation, and an explicit unresolved question. Ask another student to reproduce the decision from your notes. You are ready when they can distinguish official meaning from your analytic choice.
